open_points.subject: answer_request response id
open_points.text: The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.
open_points.other_text: The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
open_points.question: For an oversized body or a token refusal, must the body remain unread, or must it be parsed to preserve a string or integer id?

open_points.subject: run_start_sequence exception propagation
open_points.text: the first step that raises — InstallationRejectedError, RefusedError from the instance check, a store refusal, SandboxUnavailableError, StopRequiredError or any other exception — stops the sequence there and propagates unchanged to the caller with the step named in its reason
open_points.other_text: When run_start_sequence raises, MUST write the failing step and the exception's reason to standard error
open_points.question: Must an exception propagate unchanged, or may it be changed or wrapped so its reason names the failing step and serve_kernel can report that step?

open_points.subject: show_port_refs file-carriage StoredValue
open_points.text: a file carriage item becomes ShownFile with digest, size, media type, class, its value_id and no spooled_file
open_points.other_text: - StoredValue fields (exact, no others exist): value_id: str, value_digest: str, carriage: Carriage, media_type: str | None, value_schema: str, disclosure_class: DisclosureClass, size_bytes: int
open_points.question: Must a file-carriage StoredValue always have a string media_type, or must show_port_refs define how to construct the required ShownFile when media_type is None?
